author: kevaundray
content:
<@1391753260544557126> spent some more time looking at the networking that needs to be done/figured out and the unknowns and I think having leanVM depend on this poses a significant risk to the timeline, given it’s the component that all other layers depend on and there’s a lot of hardening work that needs to be done for us to have high confidence that it’s secure including making sure the proof system specs are correct (before even checking the implementation) and then starting audits

We’re now moving to hardening, but if there is a small change needed to make the difference between pq gasper and pq dc, then it sounds okay to reconsider

author: alexey_91090
content:
Yeah makes sense, totally fine to focus on hardening now

Still think we need numbers under realistic load soon though (16 committees, more aggregators, EL running alongside), so we don't find out at the last minute whether full Gasper load fits to leanVM perf

And just to check: the freeze is on the protocol/spec, not the implementation, right? If needed I can keep optimizing and test my own impl of the freezed spec

author: kevaundray
content: yeah exactly, It's a freeze on the specs and the performance of the leanVM impl being worked on in leanEthereum (so we can start to understand the prover for liveness issues)
